extension.summary: Conway's Game of Life and other cellular automata on the GPU, tuned for weak devices
extension.description:
The Cellular Automata screensaver rebuilt for devices that cannot hold a steady frame rate with the full version. It is the same GPU automaton: the whole grid lives in a texture and one shader pass makes a generation, so millions of cells can run at once. Choose from 18 rules (Conway's Life, HighLife, Day and Night, Seeds, Maze, Brian's Brain, Star Wars and more, including multi-state Generations rules) or type your own, such as B36/S125 or B2/S/C3. Start from random soup, clusters, a mirrored kaleidoscope, a single R-pentomino or acorn, four Gosper glider guns, or a swarm of gliders; it starts over by itself when the board dies out or settles.
What makes it Lite is where the time goes. The clock is optional and off to begin with, and while it is off nothing about it exists: no font is loaded, no clock texture is created, the simulation shader has no mask lookup and there is no overlay pass, so it costs exactly what a build with no clock at all does. Switch it on and the time sits in the middle -- on top, bursting into life at each change, cut out of the cells, or made of the cells themselves -- in any of the fonts, and it is drawn after the scene has been scaled up, so the digits stay sharp whatever the scene is drawn at. The simulation and drawing shaders are generated at start with the options you chose -- the rule, wrap, colour mode, clock mode, view, background, cell shape, glow and screen effect -- compiled in as constants, so none of the options you did not pick cost anything: no branches, no unused palette, mask or neighbour lookups. Wrapping the grid is one multiply and a fract per neighbour instead of a divide and a mod. The scene is drawn at no more than twice the number of cells and no more than 1080p, then scaled up once, so a 4K output costs one cheap copy pass instead of a 4K simulation view; this is the setting to lower first if the picture still stutters. Its defaults are light too: 640 x 360 cells (about 230 thousand) instead of the full version's 960 x 540 (about half a million), and the same 30 generations a second, with the automatic slow-down if the device cannot keep up.
Everything else is the same: colour by age, position or time from eight palettes, one colour, rainbow, fire, neighbour count, rainbow ghosts or plasma; trails, glow, square, rounded or dot cells, random sparks and dimming; raised, lit blocks, a landscape, a tunnel or a globe view, with a camera that drifts, zooms or flies. This build is for 32-bit Android Kodi (armeabi-v7a), as on many Google TV boxes.
extension.disclaimer: Native add-on built for Kodi 21 Omega, 32-bit ARM Android (armeabi-v7a), as on many Google TV boxes. It needs OpenGL ES 2.0 with high-precision floats in fragment shaders. The full Cellular Automata screensaver is a separate add-on; this one reaches the same features through shaders specialised for the device.
